Cube World: A Colorful and Addictive Exploration Adventure

Cube World is an indie action RPG that stands out due to its unique voxel-based world, vast exploration, and emphasis on creativity and adventure. Developed by Picroma, the game takes place in a beautifully crafted open world where everything—from the environment to the creatures—is made of colorful, blocky cubes, giving it a distinctive charm. While it was initially met with significant anticipation and a long development cycle, Cube World offers an incredibly immersive and enjoyable experience for fans of exploration and action RPGs.

At its core, Cube World is about adventure and exploration. The world is procedurally generated, meaning no two playthroughs are the same. Players can explore a massive landscape filled with forests, mountains, deserts, oceans, and dungeons. This sense of vastness and freedom is one of the game’s strongest points, as it encourages players to discover new areas, battle fierce enemies, and uncover hidden treasures.

The combat system in Cube World is dynamic and engaging. Players can choose from various classes, including Warrior, Ranger, Mage, and Rogue, each with their own unique abilities and playstyles. Whether you’re charging into battle with a sword, shooting arrows from a distance, or casting spells, the combat is fast-paced and satisfying. It’s simple enough to be accessible to newcomers but offers enough depth for players to experiment with different strategies as they progress through the game.

One of the most appealing aspects of Cube World is its focus on character progression and loot. As you explore the world and defeat enemies, you’ll gain experience points and collect a wide variety of weapons, armor, and items. These loot drops are essential to improving your character and unlocking new abilities, giving you a constant sense of progression and reward. The crafting system is also an essential part of the game, allowing players to gather materials from the environment and create new items, potions, and gear to help in their adventure.

The game’s crafting system is deep, and it allows for customization and creativity, giving players the freedom to choose how they want to approach challenges. Whether it’s crafting better armor or preparing potions for a tough boss fight, the crafting system allows for strategic planning and decision-making. This adds another layer of depth to the gameplay, making each adventure feel unique and personal.

While the world of Cube World may be simple and blocky in design, the vibrant and colorful aesthetic is one of the game’s biggest strengths. The visuals are both charming and easy on the eyes, making the exploration feel lighthearted and fun. The landscapes are diverse and beautiful, and the game’s day-night cycle, as well as its weather effects, create a dynamic world that feels alive. Whether you’re exploring a serene forest or traversing a vast desert, the visual variety keeps the game fresh and engaging.

Cube World also offers multiplayer support, allowing friends to join up and explore the world together. The cooperative aspect adds a new layer of fun, as you can team up to take on dungeons, defeat bosses, and explore the vast world more efficiently. Playing with friends also makes the world feel more dynamic and exciting, as you work together to overcome the challenges that the game presents.

Despite some of its rough edges and limited content at launch, Cube World has evolved over time with regular updates and improvements. The game’s modding community has also played a huge role in expanding the game, with numerous fan-made mods adding new content and enhancing the overall experience.

In conclusion, Cube World is an incredibly enjoyable and relaxing game that offers a refreshing take on the action RPG genre. Its focus on exploration, combat, and crafting makes it a game that rewards curiosity and creativity, while its charming voxel art and engaging mechanics keep players coming back for more. Whether you’re playing solo or with friends, Cube World provides a vast and colorful world to lose yourself in, making it a game worth experiencing for fans of open-world adventures.

I think this game got too much backlash; it was made by an already unstable dev and was initially made as a passion project between him and his wife. 

CubeWorld could've been better; it could've been an MMO or a standard RPG. Still, he chose to take a creative turn. He added zone levels and a new stage of progression, so players didn't run into the infinite loop of progression that made them so strong everything was easy to fight, or the world got stronger alongside the player, making it so no matter what you were always weak compared to most newer mobs. In no way is it a bad game now. If anything, I still come back to it; I feel like it could've been better if we kept a more open mindset when it was first released instead of instantly threatening and hurting the dev. The community made CubeWorld a bad game because it never got a chance to be fully nurtured or mended...I hope one day the developer returns to this project or even creates a new one, he deserves better, and like all talented creators, he deserves a better community.

Even though its not as good as the Alpha in my opinion, people need to seriously stop pretending like Wollay 'abandoned' the game, because that is simply a straight up lie.
He is literally working on this game on his own, and updates were always infrequent. Waiting 2 years for a social media post has been completely normal since the Alpha came out. 

People with unnecessarily harsh criticism were exactly the reason why he didn't share more about the development and why there was no real play testing of his Beta builds until the game released. He made the game the way he thought it would be fun, which is generally hard to pull off successfully when you don't have input from people who aren't developers for the game themselves (or more accurately in this case, from people who aren't literally yourself).

If you have genuine criticism for what he could have done better, feel free to write him a message on Twitter or write a review. If your criticism boils down to 'Its not as good as Alpha and he abandoned it' I'm sorry to say, but literally everyone knows its not as good game play wise and you aren't doing anybody a favour by making him even more self conscious about a project that took him literal years to even release publicly and that he has been consistently working on for over a decade.

Just because he doesn't post a weekly update for the toxic people who have no object permanence doesn't mean hes stopped working on it, it just means he isn't posting updates - as usual. Probably [i] because [/i] people keep complaining that hes not doing enough.



[b] Why its not as fun as the Alpha: [/b]

Gear is region locked and looses its stats when going to a new area of the map.
That includes all gear except the flat movement bonuses you get from Relics.
This makes grinding the game and ''leveling'' feel a bit meaningless, since there is no traditional XP system and the gear you worked for goes from OP to useless as soon as you finish fighting the areas boss. All you get to keep is move speed bonuses. A nice idea as a concept, pretty frustrating in actual game play.


[b] Why I'm still giving it a positive review: [/b]

The game has a great vibe, unique and revolutionary look that was copied dozens of times by other games, some funny dialogue and a random map generation that's amazing, especially considering only one person works on it.
Most importantly though, I'm nostalgic and hope Wollay continues his work on this game so it can become the masterpiece it could have been. Mods exist to give you a more 'Alpha' game play loop, if that's what you are looking for, and more in-depth systems like housing, better path finding and questing are being worked on, as well as an UE5 update.


In conclusion:
[list]
 [*]Is the game as good as it could (and maybe should) be?
 No.
 [*]Why are there no updates? 
Because hes a solo dev and you are impatient. Stop complaining and play another game in the meantime.
 [*]Is it worth to buy?
Probably yes, if you haven't played the Alpha and just download the mod. If you have played the Alpha you get the game for free anyways - because contrary to what toxic gamers say, Wollay actually cares.
 [*]When is the game finished?
It probably never will be.

I played this game in the Alpha version a pretty long tome ago, so I have nostalgic memories of Cube World. I played it recently and bought the steam version and here's what I have to say about Cube World in general:

I truly believe this game likely would have been a titan in the "block game" category if the creator didn't take a hard left turn when updating it past alpha to put on steam. Alpha world generation is peak world generation, the game was simple and had an addictive gameplay loop. Improving skill trees, adding human companions, improving village generation (or making a quest based generation) could have been implemented to make the game perfect.

Cube World Steam Version changes the main gameplay loop entirely. crafting materials are rarer and loot drops are better, and there is no level restriction on equipment. The new gameplay loop is kill bosses, loot better gear, kill more bosses. The objective of Steam Version is to collect "Artifacts" around the biomes which give random improvements to abilities. Leaving a biome removes all the items collected and "resets" your character. This is a literal gameplay "Loop." Once you complete the first area, you have to do the exact same thing again from the bottom. Dying in steam version also sucks. Even with gear equal to the boss, you are still extremely likely to die if you don't cheese the boss. respawn areas are 1-3 entire minutes away from boss locations, so you are stuck holding W and maybe scrolling on your phone for 3 minutes just to die immediately and do it again. This is where I stopped playing Steam Version, fighting the highest level enemy with the highest level equipment and losing multiple times. 

The alpha version is a craft/loot combination exploration game. You start out extremely weak, dying to every wild animal. Finding crafting materials and fighting the few enemies you can defeat lets you get better armor and use the very limited skill tree. Killing the bosses scattered around the map provides you with special crafting materials for weapons and a bunch of exp. As you level up, you can craft better gear and equip better gear. That is the gameplay loop of alpha Cube World. Craft and equip gear to kill difficult bosses, level up, craft more gear and fight more bosses. The distance between bosses in alpha is still obscene, but there are respawn points 15 seconds away from every boss, and the areas in between are filled out better with ore, crafting materials, and radiant bosses.

I really wish this game was moddable. Sadly, it seems that the developer made a lot of the code and programs very unfriendly to modders. The 4-5 mods for this game are not true scripted mods, but are instead mods that change 1 or 2 numbers of a variable.

Heres how I suggest enjoying cube world:

1. Buy the steam version and play it for a few hours. Don't hurt the developer because you don't like how they manage their game, they still deserve support for creating the game you are playing. 

2. Look for the alpha version download online. Download that version and play it for a few hours as well. The game is very hard in the start because everything can kill you, so don't get discouraged right off the bat. There is little skill mechanics in the game, enemies auto lock attacks, have super far reach and attack faster than you can dodge. You are required to get better equipment to defeat enemies.

So after reading all the reviews I was very sceptical about buying this game, but after playing the alpha for a few days, I wanted more, so I decided to bite the bullet and buy this full release. When I tell you I was shocked at how so much of the backlash against this game is unjustified. You would think this was a completely unplayable mess but it is so much like the alpha that I don't understand why it gets so much hate. 

The most notable difference is the levelling up system. Instead of earning xp for each kill, your progression level is tied up with the weapon and items you have equipped, and I think this makes for a unique level system that I haven't seen a lot of. There are so many more mobs that are fun to discover and the terrain is so much more varied, there are new structures, the respawn points are in little ancient Greek style temples, some even on floating islands that I haven't figured out how to get to yet (near them is an alter type structure with an eagle statue so I'm sure later when I progress more, there will be an item to activate them somehow.) And also there are a lot more wandering npc's in the world, some friendly and some foe, and this just makes the world seem more alive.

Another plus is npc's, both in towns and in the world, are actually useful to interact with. A lot of times I will speak to someone and they will add a quest to the map for an item to get or someone to save, or even just a rumour they heard, and it feels very dynamic, not just "oh here's a quest, check it off, here's your reward".

Something I noticed as a minor downside is I think the lighting as changed from the alpha, because I noticed there isn't the same hazy shadow on everything like there was in the alpha, but this is so insignificant that it isn't a reason to not like the game.

As someone who was absolutely obsessed with the alpha when it came out, I 100% recommend buying the full release. It's not that expensive, if you want to wait for it to go on sale whenever, do, but don't be fooled by all the negative reviews that are only based on nostalgia. This game came out 5 years ago and I didn't buy it on release despite waiting years because of all the backlash, and all I can think of is all the time I wasted, because Cube World is an amazingly fun game.

I will recommend with one large asterisk: play with mods. I did try it without mods first and knew beforehand what I was getting into because I did some research on the game. I never played the alpha but it seems most preferred the game in that state. Without mods there is no leveling and you are more or less restricted to a zone because of the way gear works. Yes, you can explore to your heart's content, however it is nearly fruitless because you can explore and get your gear worked up pretty nicely in zone X only for it to become useless in any other one.

The mods I have used (I found them posted in the discuss section) reintroduced leveling and a host of other things that were apparently supposed to be in the finished game. Gear is still lightly tied to zones and will suffer a downgrade when entering a new area but it doesn't become completely useless.

It is a fun game but I suspect if you aren't very interested in modding your games you will likely become bored because of stark limitations of gameplay. It is also pretty tough and you will probably have to grind out very weak mobs to get at least a couple levels before being able to do much like craft some armor and a better weapon. I haven't been using guides or anything but as a mage I found I can cheese quite a bit by staying on tree tops and using magic. Doesn't work 100% of the time as some enemy projectiles (and your own magic) can break foliage and leave you tumbling to the ground if you aren't careful. You can almost fly (better than using a Hang Glider you find) by using your float ability: jump, hit float, then rapidly tap it as you sail in a direction you want. It keeps you fairly horizontal in the direction you wish to go.

The greatest aspect of this game is the dev's dedication to a seemingly lost cause. This game, originally, came at a time where minecraft was it. Lets plays not only riddled youtube but twitch and the internet collectively. But the cube aspect of the sandbox world is about where the similarities end. I find the voxel based rpg to be refreshing especially from someone who grew up on minecraft and was thankful enough to stumble upon this game during its original release. It has its flaws, no doubt about it. But I am consistently excited whenever i read about a new update or development that is coming. Every so often I download it once more, giving it a solid go. To this day however I find the pacing of the game to be slow and drawn out. The sandbox aspect gives you the freedom to do as you wish but it is limited enough that you have to follow a rather short list of achievements.  It can feel repetitive in this sense as it is limited in the progression systems and lack meaningful quests. The combat is incredibly fun even if it lacks complexity. The lack of depth in the story leaves players filling in the blanks, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. Despite its potential cube world often feels more like a promising concept rather than a completed game. Much of the original hype for myself and many others dwindle with long update wait times and unfinished features. 

However Picroma, or Wollay's dedication to the game is what I find most admirable. Between him and his wife Sarah i hope to see this project live to it's true potential. :)

That being said if you are willing to mod, read the history and decide if you are willing to buy into the possibility of the creator updating and improving the game, I've been following this since 2013 so I feel personally invested in it's continuation and improvement.

The pre stream release version of the game were better in a lot of ways in my experience. The version available on Steam is still a lot of fun to play and I would’ve been happy to pay the full price on Steam, but all the better that the developer provided Steam keys for existing players. 

Doing a co op world went a long way to smooth over any poor spots like excessive or aimless travel required to find new points of interest or important gear. My friend and I collected basically everything from the initial region and were able to grind out the bosses with enough persistence and kiting strategies. Some of the dungeons, etc. would have been more difficult than they were worth if I was solo and may have led me to abandon playing the game prematurely.

The biggest problem and reason my play time stopped abruptly after the first region was losing access to all the relics, especially the travel ones like the hang glider, that I had tracked down. I was not interested in restarting with nothing at that point and became disinterested in playing further.
Just wandering the completed region was more fun to me beside I enjoyed traveling via the great I’d collected, but I ran out of incentive/ new locations to explore.

That initial world and my time with the non steam version easily got my moneys worth even with the limited repeatability of its content. Just a shame that a game so focused on procedural generation didn’t lead to more longevity. 

I recommend the game with the following disclaimers/cons:
-clarity can be lacking inside the game, so searching online for answers was occasionally required to understand item combos etc.
-the game is better suited for co op play than solo
-there are significant diminishing returns are continuing to play beyond the first reason besides progress basically resets.
-early game travel is a slog that is only redeemed was the right gear is acquired to increase pace of exploration.
-there’s an air of incompleteness to the game still that requires extra effort to work around and takes me out of the immersion the game can have.

In contrast, here’s my favorite aspects/pros:
-game aesthetic was immersive and enjoyably peaceful. Just ambling through the world was a nice experience early on. I still did this occasionally after travel picked up.
-late game travel and combat throughout my play through were consistently fun to engage with. Occasionally, enemy scaling felt a bit off in both directions.
-The npc towns, friendly travelers, and tamale animals were endearing. Very cute visuals. The speech sound effect brought a decent amount of nostalgia for older rpgs.
-The game does open world well. The quests and map offer clear enough milestones to work towards, but I felt entirely free to just explore and do content in whatever order I wanted. (That non linear nature might be responsible for the scaling I remarked on.)

The game kind of feels like spending an extended period of time decompressing in a secluded woodlands cabin. It’s a great palette cleanser for other high octane / challenging games, but also has aspects like the combat to keep me engaged when I wanted something more. It doesn’t really do anything exceptionally unique and better than other options, but the combination of all the good bits make a game that continues to interest me over the years, even if I don’t actually play it as much as other great games at its price point.

Cube World is a beautiful and charming game. 
As you begin there's a depth of mystery. 

You accidentally drink your potion before you've even truly begun your journey. 
You set out to kill the nearest cute little creature, and it obliterates you with the force of a semi-truck.

You realize there is no XP bar, you may begin to lose hope and feel scammed, as if your puppy had been killed in a car accident.

You continue forward to see what this new Cube World has to offer.
You fight new enemies, face new challenges, and see new structures you've never seen before.

You find yourself your first 5 star weapon! You start to destroy everything with ease, and feel like a god.
Then you travel to the next region, and get curb stomped into the ground.
You look at your weapon and armor, and realize it's actually all trash tier in this new region.

You go back to the original region so that way your gear has any meaning, and find your first dungeon.
You explore an interesting new area, eventually make your way to the main boss, and defeat him relatively easily.
Ooh, what's this? A shiny new relic!

You delight in the reward, until you realize that all this effort was to obtain a minuscule and unnoticeable improvement to your lamp's radius.

"This game is trash" you might be thinking. However, if you get 10 more relics, if you're lucky you could get actually 4% increase to your lamp's radius. Don't worry, some day you will get a 10% increase to your lamp's radius!

I have mixed feelings about Cube World, but would say that the positive aspects of the game outweigh the issues.

Pros:
- An open world with lots of biomes, mobs, structures & fitting background music
- A cheerful artstyle and a clear UI (though scaling for higher resolutions than 1080p would be appreciated)
- Multiple classes with different playstyles, each having their strenghts & weaknesses
- Fights are fun (unless your enemy is too overpowered)
- You really feel progress in your strength as you clear a biome

Cons:
- You usually have named locations all over the world, but it's not always clear what to do there. Sometimes I spent half an hour scanning every inch of a forest or hill where (supposedly) an item must be hidden, but it's just too hard to find.
- Finding locations that match your weapon & armor level can take a long time, and sometimes there is not enough of them to get strong enough for higher level areas.
- Without a boat/glider/pet, it sometimes takes looong to get where you want to get (though you could use the flight master in every village instead of walking)
- The region-independent buffs from artefacts are too weak IMO, and should be adjusted to e.g. provide additional strength or armor.
Loved the original, this version has changes I don't like but overall the game is great. Waiting for the next update soon.

I had followed this since 2011, and backed it as soon as the shop was up. I managed to get a copy during the DDoS attack, and like many others I enjoyed the Alpha quite a bit.

Nearly 10 years later (2 years after the "full" release)... And it's just not any fun compared to the Alpha. The Alpha was released in 2013. In the 6 years between the Alpha and release, most of the features people enjoyed had been removed, and replaced with absolutely awful systems that made even the most vocal backers just give up on the project.

The Alpha released around the same time as the wave of early access survival scams, and it seems to have taken the same fate: Abandoned by a developer that ghosted on the fanbase and his product that people were paying for, and leaving it a broken and unfinished mess that could have been so much more. It's one thing to create a passion product, it's another thing to take money for it and provide the illusion there is active development going on. 

I completely understand the mental health issues that Wallay deals with, but this project is one of the most mismanaged games I can think of.  Going through with a product for sale, feeding the public enough breadcrumbs to keep interest and KNOWINGLY building on growing hype over years and years... And then blaming it on pre-existing mental health conditions is not just a copout, it's ignoring your own issues and using it as a crutch to excuse why you're not working on something you're selling to people. If you need to work on your personal mental health and emotional wellbeing, PLEASE do so. But again, don't use that as a way to scam people, because that's exactly the story of Cube World. 

It's 2022, and since 2013 the entire project shows less than a year of actual development. The developer, Wallay, has gone silent again, and spent more time ghosting the playerbase than he ever did showing signs of active development. 

For all realistic intents and purposes, this is dead.

Honestly, the fact that the dev has gone MIA not once, but twice now should be reason enough to avoid Cube World, but I'll cover what I can so that this review isn't as complete a waste of your time as the game it covers is at the time of writing.

So initially Cube World was actually pretty damn good, I played the alpha with a few of my friends on and off back when I was in high school and we all had a blast with it. However, it kind of stagnated after a while, with no news regarding upcoming updates (seriously, the only update I can really remember was the addition of an extra world boss, but like I had to go looking to find any news regarding it... and I'm not even sure if world bosses are still a thing in the current build) or when any of the features promised would be implemented. So yeah, it slowly died.

Then last year we suddenly heard from the dev again, Cube World was leaving alpha and with the beta build the game would also be coming to Steam! I got rather excited over this, as I hadn't played the game in a very long time and I was hyped to see it back from the dead. Unfortunately that feeling didn't last. The beta build of Cube World didn't seem to bring many majorly beneficial changes to the game, and for every step forwards taken, there were 50 more steps taken in the opposite direction. The biggest change made (and the most divisive one within the community from what I understand) was the overhaul of the progression system. Items are now tied to the region you obtained them in more or less, and become borderline unusable once you leave the region... giving you very little reason to venture out and explore, [i]in an open world game about exploration with a procedurally generated map[/i]. Skill trees have been removed from the game and gear is now much more integral to your progression, which just worsens the previously mentioned issue of gear ceasing to function the moment you cross an invisible line between regions.

Myself and a couple of mates also found the early game incredibly rough, as enemies too high level for you to physically deal damage to would seemingly spawn more frequently than those you can actually hurt in the [b]starting area[/b] making it impossible to actually get any gear, what's worse is that I personally was only able to find one item my character could actually equip out of the few drops I had managed to obtain, as the others were all for different classes.

The game has a few flaws, my [i]personal "favourite"[/i] (ignoring scuffed progression) of which being that the rogue classes invisibility doesn't actually do anything other than make you move slower, as enemies can and will still attack you or aggro onto you as if you were fully visible. The worst part about that is you are unable to change into any of the sub-classes so you can have an ability that isn't a useless cloak until you reach the first city, which requires you to defeat a boss, which first requires you to gear up, which itself requires you to defeat enemies who likely will be too high level for you.

Honestly, if the games dev would just communicate with his community rather than retreating back to his cave every time something doesn't go his way the game would likely be in a better state, or at least the community would be a bit more patient with the guy. But unfortunately he leaves us in the dark, like it's been a year since this game came out on steam and we still haven't heard anything since then.

I cannot in good faith recommend anyone to buy this game. Avoid it like the plague unless major changes are made or the dev breaks his apparent vow of silence.

EDIT: Surprise, surprise, Wollay has dissappeared once again. Since the 2019 release, there has been 0 updates, 0 patches, 0 news, 0 communication. Between the alpha and the 2019 release, 6 years have passed, if you should expect any update before another 6 year mark at the very least, then sorry to burst any bubbles.

TIPS FOR MAKING PERFECT FETTUCCINE ALFREDO:
1. Start by bringing water to a boil in a large pot. Add salt to the water to season the pasta. Once it is boiling, add pasta and cook according to package instructions.

Instructions
1. In a large pot, heat water over high heat until boiling. Add salt to season the water. Once it is boiling, add fettuccine and cook according to package instructions.

2. In a large skillet or pan, heat butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Stir in heavy cream.

3. Let heavy cream reduce and cook for 5 to 8 minutes. Add half of the parmesan cheese to the mixture and whisk well until smooth. Keep over heat and whisk well until cheese is melted.

Recipe Notes

The released version of the game is awful. I played the game back in 2013 before it was removed from Picroma's website and had high hopes for the full release. Wollay's bizarre strategy of removing the game from stores for almost a decade was a terrible one. He worked on the game sure, but with no player feedback. It's a game designed for him and him alone. The game is visually stunning that's for sure. That's about all it has going for it in it's current state.

The progression system is awful. Earning XP, leveling up, as well as the Skill Point system were all pruned from the game. The current progression system has you grinding gear like am ARPG, with the caviot of that gear being literally useless outside of the zone it is acquired in. I think this has an interesting Philosophy behind it, but when the game is focused around exploration and finding new zones, it feels terrible. You can spend a dozen hours grinding out the perfect set with just the stats you want, but if cross an invisible boundary you might as well have nothing equipped. This makes the game feel pointless. There is no point in killing ANYTHING in the open world. Enemies do not give XP, rarely ever drop items, and the items they do drop are low quality. So you spend most of the game just avoiding everything. The world feels hollow. The only way to get gear is by going to towns, talking to NPCs until they give you a map location to clear. The skill point system in the Alpha was atleast interesting as you could tailor your character towards a specific build, whereas in the full version of the game, the only improvements you can make to your character are how hard and fast you can auto attack.

Another thing of note is the difficulty of the game. There is no tutorial in game and very limited UI. The default UI has your only ability cooldown tucked into the bottom left corner of the screen, when your health, MP, and your focus are all going to be towards the center. You spawn in the wild right after making your character which is pretty flush and seamless, but if you're a new player, you'll quickly come to realize you don't know what to do. Again, this gives me the impression this is just Wollay's personal game that no one else is supposed to enjoy, let alone play. Any friend I've had try the game has quit within two hours of playing it due to the terrible new player experience. The enemy AI is terribly overpowered. Ranged and magic using enemies literally cannot miss so combat revolves around doing more damage to them before they kill you. The final nail in the coffin for me was the boomerang enemies. When they throw their boomerang, it has aggressive tracking and hardly ever misses, even with immunity frames while rolling. If and when it connects it doesn't return but instead glues onto your character doing constant damage for around 5 seconds. It only takes 2 boomerang throws to kill a newly created character. If your character is a boomerang user, it functions much differently to the point where you question if your boomerang is just cosmetic. Magic uses suffer a similar issue when they cast a tornado spell it moves along with the character they're targeting causing it to never miss, whereas when your character can cast tornado spells if you move your mouse even slightly the entire spell cancels. Somehow Wollay made the enemy AI worse to the point of being irredeemable.

It's really sad that the limited Alpha version of the game feels like it's had much more work and love put into it than the full release version with almost a decade to get the vision down. I hope Wollay reads some feedback for once and gets this game on track. It has a lot going for it. It's gorgeous and the core RPG concepts themselves have potential. It's sad that this review has to be negative. During the alpha, the game was great, it has great gameplay, great progression, great customizability thanks to the skill tree and much more.

[b]And then the beta came[/b]

In the beta, there were [i]a couple changes to the game[/i]. First of all, the ENTIRE map was visible from the start, so you could see where you were going. They improved the quest system, which is great. Aaaaand that basically all the good parts. You could no longer level up through XP, and instead level up by collecting artifacts. Level ups however have been made useless. The only thing you gain from leveling up is a small boost to one random Utility-stat (i.e different kinds of movement). The skill tree was gone, completely. They have also basically removed any kind of meaningful permanent progression. Now saying that probably makes you ask: "Well, at least my equipment is permanent and always usable, no matter when or where I am in the game.". And if you asked that, then you're wrong. All equipment (besides pets) you find is Region-bound, meaning they will only work in the area that you found them in. So if you find a legendary sword in one area, then it basically becomes a common when entering a new area. There is ONE exception, and that is that if you find a item bound to RegionName+, it will also work properly when used in a neighbouring area. All key items you find (gliders, boats, harps, saddles etc) are [b]also[/b] region-bound, however these items can't be "+" items.

Overall I would have to say this is not a bad game. Its gameplay loop is fairly shallow, but not entirely unsatisfying. There are definitely things in the game that show immense promise if worked on. I finished one area in a little under 6 hours, and as I went to the next area I found myself completely unmotivated by the sense of progression. The fact that there's very little long-term reward for beating an area means your progression constantly gets reset every 5 hours or so. The artifacts that carry over have small gameplay effects and are largely not worth it. Overall the alpha version of the game had a better sense of progression despite its grindy nature. 

The problem, as I see it, is that even though the developer has access to a fairly large player-base, he doesn't use them for feedback. It seems like they shut themselves off from everyone for years to work on the game because they had a hard time with some of the more inflammatory "criticism" leveled at the game by "The Gamers™" As a result they game was developed in a vacuum without any community having the ability to give feedback on what they do and don't like. This means they got to design the game they wanted to design, but it also means that since what they wanted and what the community wanted were largely different, it led to players being disappointed that the game went in a completely different direction than what it seemed to be heading for in alpha.

TL:DR- 4/10. Has some cool and fun aspects, but is largely mediocre and unsatisfying. Buy it if it's on sale.

ABOUT THIS GAME
What is Cube World?
Cube World is a voxel-based action RPG with a focus on exploration. It takes place in a procedurally generated fantasy world made up entirely of cubes.
Features
Choose between four different classes: Warrior, Ranger, Mage, Rogue.
Action-based combat with dodging, aiming, combos, special skills and more.
Explore a nearly infinite, procedurally generated fantasy world.
Plan your next adventure with the 3D voxel world map. Scroll and zoom everywhere to find your next destination!
Craft weapons, armor, potions, elixirs and food and more from ingredients found throughout the world.
Tame pets that fight along your side and can be used as mounts.
Non-linear, open world gameplay. Solve quests, help residents, fight huge monsters, explore ancient dungeons! It's all up to you!
Discover procedurally generated lore and learn about ancient civilizations and magic artifacts.
Retrieve unique magic artifacts to level up and improve your skills.
Earn gold to buy items or to book an eagle flight to new lands.
Cube World's unique per-land progression system makes finding loot, solving quests and clearing dungeons rewarding and exciting over and over again.
Use your hang glider to take to the skies or explore the oceans with your boat.
Find magic items to enter secret areas and to support you on your journey.
Play solo singleplayer or join your friends in coop-online-multiplayer.

So sad to see the release version of Cube World in this state. I've played for a bit over an hour before installing mods and having more fun as a result. The base game does not reward the player in any meaningful way. You are supposed to explore regions, collect some "lore" and find artifacts that permanently buff your character. Now it would be a fun thing to do, but:
1 - the so called "exploration" is completely removed from the equation because the world IS NOT randomly generated, only the player's initial spawn point is randomized, so the map is fully accessible to you to look around and mark anything on it that looks like points of interest. It is so much easier to look at the map for like 5-10 minutes and mark everything in the region and then just run around and complete everything in a few hours
2 - the artifacts don't provide ANY useful buffs for your character (lamp light range, swimming/gliding speed etc.) and even then the buffs are in the range of 1% per artifact. Not to mention, some buffs are completely broken and don't affect the stats they're supposed to.
3 - the equipment is region-locked. Let me repeat, ALL EQUIPMENT YOU GET IS ONLY USEFUL IN A REGION YOU GET IT IN, THE MOMENT YOU MOVE TO A DIFFERENT REGION IT ALL BECOMES USELESS. There is a tiny chance you get a special marked equipment that does not get debuffed outside its origin region, but those are ridiculously rare and you don't ever target getting such gear since it is completely up to your luck whether you get it or not. Oh also the exploration equipment is region-locked as well. That means if you suddenly move from one ocean region to another, you get dismounted from your boat because you haven't found it in a new ocean. F U N 

So the ACTUAL gameplay loop is: stare at the map for a few minutes and mark everything that looks interesting, do a mad dash for all the points of interest (the only somewhat fun part of the vanilla experience), pray you get glider and the boat early on and decent equipment along the way to not get stuck on one place for long, get absolutely useless artifacts and move on to a next region, repeat until the end of times.

The game sabotages itself on every step of its fun-on-paper gameplay loop, thus completely removing any sense of player's global progression, resetting them to basically zero every single time.

I hate this game. More specifically, I hate this release of the game. They were on the right track when initially creating this game. The alpha for Cube World had a big world (with a fixed size) that had a lot of secrets, biomes and cool stuff to explore and find, kind-of like Terraria. The problem was that once you got to the end of the game, nothing really happened. You could keep searching for dungeons and getting infinite levels, but there was no proper "infinite content" for people to enjoy.

This game tried to solve the problem of endgame content. Every skill/ability starts as unlocked for every class now. Once you finish all the quests in an area, you have to go to a new randomly generated area and your stats all reset. You don't feel like you're getting powerful, instead you're appeasing some random farmers and in return you're allowed to not get killed instantly by random cow monsters while in a specific region. It's not MMO progression, it's just random quests with hollow useless rewards. And players don't even have any skill progression. Even the items that allow for faster travel are area-restricted for some reason.

In my opinion, the developer should have instead kept the entire alpha functionality alive, but extended the world like Noita does. If they want stats to be dependent on region, that's fine. The developer should have just made the regions HUGE enough for people to feel like they're actually progressing. The entire game should  fit into a region, because traversing regions and losing progress is such a massive punch to the gut. 

And progression should still include skills/abilities, because they are such an important thing for players to look forward to on the player's path. The game could just reset a player's level while keeping their skills while they transition to a new "alternate world", or something analogous. It's nuts that really beloved MMO game mechanics were pointlessly thrown away in the full release.

To me, this game is a huge example of how miscommunication and fundamental misunderstanding of the playerbase's expectations can lead to a significantly inferior end product. It's so tragic because all the core ideas were solid, but the implementation just didn't account for how the players (who love MMO grind gameplay) would feel about being locked into tiny boxes for using any of their loot and stats.

What a sad, sad story. I hope the developers stay motivated and revive this game into what it could be, in all its glory, one day. Or maybe another developer will pick up the mantle. Who knows. As it stands, I cannot recommend this game, unless you enjoy your progress being wiped every time you walk into a new biome for a change of scenery. Instead, I suggest tracking down the Alpha version of the game and playing that.

That said, the developer is occasionally still working on the game. I am cautiously optimistic that we will receive fixes to the current system, eventually.. Once that happens, I will change this review to be positive. Hey Wollay, if you happen to read this, please remove the region-locking system until you've changed the scale to be orders of magnitude bigger, encompassing entire WoW-scale continents or something bigger. Or, until that change, just replace the Steam version with the Alpha build. I would legitimately still be happy with the game if we just had the alpha build and nothing else.

Cube World is an Open-World, voxel based game with RPG elements. Play as your favourite class, explore the word, fight monsters and delve dungeons. Level up and become great. Unfortunately this is all just noise in the aether. The game never lived up to its stated goal. Not even close. The developer never delivered more than the initial demo. TWICE.

When this game was first released, Minecraft was in its heyday but what a lot of people wanted was a game engine like Minecraft, but with RPG elements added. This is where Cube World entered. The promises were great. Character development, open world exploration, multiplayer dungeon crawling in a simple voxel environment. Unfortunately after the initial release a just a few minor updates, development went dark and no further updates were received. The game was dead.

Fortunately the developer finally came back (years later) with updates, plans, enthusiasm and more. Unfortunately this was all just wind. The game was re-released in a dumbed-down format with even less functionality. Once again the developer went dark, closed shop and stopped providing updates or even feedback.

Those of us that had hope that this might be a great game were fooled twice - but not three times. In truth the game no longer has the relevance it one might have had. Had it been followed up on when originally released it may have been huge - even to rival Minecraft. Today it's just one of a number of voxel or cube based open-world games with RPG elements; and a bad one at that.

What could have been a groundbreaking game ended up as one of the biggest gaming “what-ifs” of all time. Let’s break down this pixelated disappointment.

[b][u]Graphics: 7/10[/u][/b]
Visually, Cube World is charming. Its voxel art style is undeniably cute, and the world is colorful and inviting. It’s the kind of game that looks like a cross between Minecraft and an RPG dreamland. But looks can only carry you so far, especially when the rest of the game is as empty as a promise from a bad Kickstarter campaign.

[b][u]Gameplay: 5/10 (Because It Technically Exists)[/u]
The core gameplay of Cube World had potential. You’ve got exploration, combat, crafting, and a sprawling open world to dive into. But that’s about where the excitement ends. The game feels hollow—like someone built a beautiful stage and forgot to write the script.

Combat is repetitive, progression is slow, and for a game that promised infinite adventure, it somehow manages to feel lifeless. There’s just not enough to do, and what is there quickly wears thin.

[b][u]Development: 2/10 (AKA The Real Story Here)[/u]
This is where things get tragic. Cube World was hyped up by its creator, Wolfram von Funck, as a revolutionary RPG experience. The alpha release in 2013 showed incredible promise, and fans rallied around the game, eagerly awaiting updates. But instead of building on the foundation, the game disappeared into development limbo for years.

When Cube World finally resurfaced in 2019 with an official release, it was a shell of what players had hoped for. Features were missing, mechanics felt half-baked, and the magic was gone. It’s like waiting years for your favorite band’s reunion album, only to discover it’s 30 minutes of static.

[b][u]Exploration: 6/10[/u][/b]
Exploration is one of Cube World’s saving graces. The world is vast, procedurally generated, and packed with little nooks and crannies to discover. But even this gets old fast. Without meaningful content to fill the world, exploration feels like wandering through a beautiful but empty art gallery.

[b][u]Soundtrack: 8/10[/u][/b]
If there’s one thing Cube World did right, it’s the music. The soundtrack is soothing, atmospheric, and perfectly complements the game’s whimsical aesthetic. It’s the kind of music you’d put on in the background while doing literally anything other than playing the game.

[b][u]Final Verdict: 5/10[/u][/b]
Cube World is a cautionary tale of hype, promise, and missed opportunities. What could have been a genre-defining game ended up as a forgotten relic of over-ambition and under-delivery. For the few hours it’s fun, the game is a reminder of what might have been. But for those who invested years of hope? It’s a bittersweet disappointment.

If you’re curious, give it a try. Just don’t expect to find the epic RPG adventure you were promised. And if you’re one of those people still waiting for a meaningful update? Well, I’ve got some bad news.

But then Wollay didn't communicate with us for years, barely giving us scraps here and there in the form of a screenshot every six months to two years.

Then the full game came out and it's horrible. The world still feels empty. Region locking gear is an okay concept with terrible execution. He made the excuse of mental health as to why he didn't communicate, and while mental health is important, it doesn't stop anyone else from producing a good game and many people are capable of turning their fear, depression and passions into a good game, I.E. Celeste and Binding of Isaac.

The game is beautiful. Some people enjoy the game just for wandering around taking in the world generation. But if you want actual combat, gameplay, progression, or any other aspect besides procedural world generation, look elsewhere. 

You start out with nothing, you explore and kill some innocent animals, find a town, talk to NPCs and they will tell you of some dungeon locations. Go to those dungeons, find out they're too hard for you, get annihilated, go to easier dungeons. Get some basic gear, explore, "mine" AKA get lucky finding a rock in a cave or mountain and destroy it with your weapon, upgrade your gear through the game's unique modification system, collect items and slowly work your way up through harder dungeons until you can take on the region's hardest dungeons. If you clear those dungeons, you get an artifact which gives you a small permanent stat boost, even when going to a new region. Now, up to this point, the game is actually pretty damn fun. But when you go to a new region, you'll notice that all your gear that you worked on will be ineffective and you have to start over with a minimal permanent upgrade to your stats. And when I say minimal, imagine spending ten hours playing a game and the only true progression you earn is that you can climb 1% faster. Then you go to a new area where you must start from scratch so you can spend another 10 hours to climb 2% faster. Yes, it's that bad. The game cycle hypes you up just to destroy you. It builds you up two-fold so it can break you down ten-fold.

I would highly advise waiting for a decent voxel adventure game like Veloren, but if you really must buy this game and give a cruddy developer your money, it is somewhat salvageable with mods. There are mods that improve or remove region locking altogether, improve the artifact stat bonus, and make the game generally less awful. The game is not abandoned, but it might as well be. Wollay is still leaving scraps in the form of replying to one email every six months and providing a screenshot once every ten blue moons. The game left a giant cube-shaped hole in many people's hearts that I don't know will ever be filled. An absolute tragedy and a perfect example why communication is key.

There's a lot of reviews out there that are too short and don't really explain much, so I figured I'd leave a review here with better details.

Cube world Alpha was released in July of 2013 and had a functioning level system with Stat point allocation. The stat points affected your adventure based on how you played such as increasing the speed of your glider, boat or how fast you moved when riding your pet. It added a lot of sandbox-style freedom with the RPG-playstyle and honestly was a lot of fun. The developer of the game announced the Alpha would receive no updates while the finished game was developed, then completely dropped off the face of the earth. He released the occasional "Progress Update" on his twitter, but refused to listen to community feedback. Since the release of the full game on Steam, the developer has once again gone radio silent and seemingly vanished.

As we've seen all too many times in the gaming industries, developers ignoring community feedback never pans out well. The games are poorly received, and rated as such. Unfortunately Cube World became one of those games, with the removal of nearly all features of Alpha that made the game fun. It was streamlined, way over-simplified, and the "progression" system was both lazy and also a terrible attempt at stretching the content of the game out. The world generation is split into regions, with gear farmed from enemies or world events. This gear is region-locked, meaning all the time you spend in a region farming powerful gear doesn't carry over into other regions. Upon crossing into the new region, the gear from the old region is nerfed and becomes bottom-tier. It only works in the region it was looted from. The "Artifact" progression promotes adventure with promises of steadily making your character more powerful, but falls terribly short with its promise with very little actual benefit to your stats.

Cube World suffered immensely from the poor decision of ignoring the community, and the release of the full game is a shadow of its former self. On its own, I do not recommend the game unless you truly enjoy starting over in every region. The game was saved by the mod community, and without them I doubt the game could even maintain a "mixed" review of 44% positive votes.

Unless you plan on modding the game, it's not worth the buy.

What can I say... 
A decade ago I played and loved the alpha for endless hours. 
When it was announced that Cube World would be developed further, I was beside myself with joy and waited for years for the full version to be released. 
But unfortunately everything turned out very differently. 
Instead of leaving the game as it was and simply improving existing features (more skills, more classes, expanding crafting, mining and placing blocks, etc.), the basic principle behind the game was changed. 
Originally you leveled up by gaining XP from killing enemies, but in the full version levels are determined by how many artifacts a player has collected. 
Artifacts are obtained through dungeons, bosses and treasures and give minor buffs.
Another strange change is that the skill tree has been removed and skills like Riding, Gliding and Sailing are now completely tied to equipment that you have to find in a region to unlock the skill instead of getting it through the skill tree.
Also, this equipment is region-bound, meaning that if you leave a region, you lose it (glider, boat, etc.) and have to find it again in the new region.
For me and probably many others, the change to the game is a very disappointing change.
We liked the game the way it was, so why change it?

[Summary]
The gameplay of the alpha version was changed in the full version

Alpha:
- Level up through XP grinding by killing enemies
- Unlock and improve skills by leveling up

Full version:
- Level up by collecting artifacts

6 Years of waiting after being ghosted several times by the game developer. 6 Years is what it took for the game to stop agonizing and finally dying.

During development, Wollay decided what was better for the players: No level progression and a region lock. 

Although I like the game itself and I become addicted any time I play it, I can't play this version without modding it. How is it possible, that 6 years of game development feel like a massive downgrade? When it comes to the gameplay:

-Respawning:

It is a pain to respawn, and as many of you will probably know, there are a bunch of checkpoints in the map that can be enabled for teleporting and respawning there. But here's the issue: You die. A lot. Just by fighting the most basic enemies. The spawn shrines are pretty much far away from anything important most of the time and you will have to take your time to go back after dying every single time. 

-Progression:

There is little to none. Progression as of now consists of just exploring while trying not to get destroyed by enemies. At first you're pretty harmless. You're either very lucky and find a 5-star weapon that deals a ton of damage, or take your time slowly grinding with 3-star gear, 4-star gear and so on. When you get new gear, your stats get high as if you were leveling, but your level will still be the same. You only level up by completing regions, and it's pretty useless. With the region lock applied, your gear is rendered useless when you enter a new region. Hand glider and boat disappear as well. There is a region lock fix mod that gets rid of this, and the game is very enjoyable that way. 

-Grinding and region lock:

This was the worst problem. It means having to begin from scratch any time you go to a new region to explore. You have to find a few items to progress, and it can take many hours. Problem with this is, exploring is not fun anymore as you're forced to do so. Entering a new region can be painful and repetitive when there are enemies nearby, as they will kill you in one hit or two, and you can do nothing about it. I kept repeating this with a friend until we just stopped trying and went to play something else. 

-The map:

There is no seed anymore. You appear at some random place and good luck. I don't like this, and I still don't know how it works. All I know is that after playing a bit with friends they were all in the same map, but thousands of chunks away. 

Overall, this game is enjoyable if you play alone and use mods. Or if you go back to the alpha, which had a somewhat decent leveling system. But don't buy it. Don't give more money to this developer, he doesn't deserve it.

I've wanted to enjoy this so bad since it launched on steam but it's just so annoyingly bad.

For starters, there is no clear cut leveling system. All of your stats are tied to your gear that you find/craft. There's no experience points and no abilities or talents to work towards unlocking. The latter isn't necessarily bad, but having access to all your class abilities from the start is slightly boring.
It's an RPG with no skills to unlock. it feels weird.

The enemy scaling is terrible. You could start a new character, see some bugs in the distance you think you can take on and then be dead 10 seconds after attacking them. 

Your gear is region locked. If you enter a new zone you have to re-obtain special equipment (boat, glider, etc.) for that zone and all of your gear gets downgraded. Did you spend a long time obtaining/crafting the best gear you could? Better get ready to do it all over again cause it will be useless if you enter a new region! And because your stats are tied to your gear (since there's no exp based leveling system) you're basically level 1 when you enter a new region!

Traveling becomes kind of annoying after a while. You will either need to find and tame a ride-able pet to speed you up or spend gold on flight paths.

Good luck trying to progress if its night time in game. This game is so unreasonably dark you cannot see anything. Your lantern does not provide enough light. Oh, and there is no brightness setting to crank up to get around this issue. So there's that.

Word gen customization. In the Alpha version of the game you could enter custom seeds for your world generation which was neat. That feature is gone now in this version. There aren't even world slots for you to use. It just assigns a world to your character and that's that.

This game had such potential to be amazing. A lot of people loved the alpha release, but the developer took so many steps in the wrong direction with this.

Don't buy the game. Not worth it unless the dev comes back from the dead to finish it.
If you really want to play it though, make sure you mod it. I recommend trying CubeMegaMod. It's one of the few mods that are still compatible with the game.
